ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Flannery O'Connor

code.originalText: Three-month response assessment for lupus nephritis and glucocorticoid taper

text.paragraph: Ms. O'Connor is thirteen weeks into treatment. Her joint pain and swelling settled within three weeks and the facial rash has faded with sun protection; she has had no fevers. She takes prednisone 10 mg a day, reached a month ago, mycophenolate 1000 mg twice daily (loose stools in the first two weeks, since settled), weekly belimumab by her own injection, hydroxychloroquine, and losartan. The rheumatology blood counts, weekly for the first month and twice monthly since, have stayed normal, with white cells between 4.8 and 7.9 and normal liver tests. The bladder infection in June grew Escherichia coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin and cleared after seven days. Her baseline eye examination a month ago was normal. She has gained 3.4 kg and sleeps less well on the days after a dose reduction. She writes five mornings a week. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-07-27; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; slight fullness of the face
No malar rash; no mouth ulcers
No synovitis; full, painless hip movement

Pain and swelling of the small joints of both hands, the wrists, and the knees for three months, with an hour of morning stiffness, evening fevers to 38 °C, fatigue, and a red rash over the cheeks and nose after sun; told elsewhere it might be rheumatoid arthritis; cause to be established

S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus at the second visit; joint pain in 1950 with suspected rheumatoid arthritis is documented (D).
Protein and blood in the urine: protein-to-creatinine ratio 1.6 g/g and 18 red cells per high-power field, with normal creatinine; cause to be established
S — Synthetic presenting finding at the index visit, superseded by the kidney biopsy diagnosis at the third visit.

Systemic lupus erythematosus, classified by the EULAR/ACR criteria (ANA 1:640 homogeneous; score 32 before the biopsy): inflammatory arthritis, acute cutaneous lupus (malar rash), fever, leukopenia with lymphopenia, mild thrombocytopenia, low C3 and C4, anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm positive; antiphospholipid antibodies and lupus anticoagulant negative
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis and results; her systemic lupus erythematosus, diagnosed in Atlanta in late 1950 or early 1951, is documented (D), but no finding from her lifetime is used.

Lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS class III (A), focal proliferative, on kidney biopsy: endocapillary proliferation in 9 of 30 glomeruli, activity index 6 of 24, chronicity index 1 of 12, full-house immunofluorescence; no thrombotic microangiopathy; urine protein-to-creatinine ratio 1.8 g/g; normal kidney function
S — Synthetic biopsy result and class; kidney involvement is documented at the end of her life, but no kidney finding from her lifetime is used.
Long-term glucocorticoid treatment for lupus nephritis, tapering to 5 mg a day or less
S — Synthetic treatment status; the documented steroid harm in her life is the reason the episode keeps glucocorticoids low.
Long-term mycophenolate mofetil, with belimumab, for lupus nephritis; bone and infection protection in place
Levonorgestrel intrauterine system for highly effective contraception during mycophenolate treatment
S — Synthetic contraception, chosen by the patient.

Acute cystitis on mycophenolate, belimumab, and prednisone 15 mg: two days of burning, frequency, and urgency without fever or flank pain; urine culture grew Escherichia coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin; resolved with seven days of nitrofurantoin
S — Synthetic common infection in an immunosuppressed young woman; coded without hematuria because the persistent hematuria is from her nephritis.

list.item:
Class III lupus nephritis on treatment (M32.14). The protein-to-creatinine ratio has halved, from 1.8 to 0.9 g/g, with fewer red cells (6 per high-power field) and stable creatinine 0.8. Anti-dsDNA has fallen from 186 to 72 and complements are rising (C3 84, C4 13). She is responding and on track for a complete response. [S]
Continue mycophenolate 1000 mg twice daily, belimumab weekly, hydroxychloroquine, and losartan.
Prednisone to 7.5 mg next month and 5 mg by six months.
Blood counts monthly from now.

Systemic lupus erythematosus (M32.19). Clinically quiet outside the kidney. Cardiovascular risk: LDL 128 mg/dL, total cholesterol 212, HDL 58 on prednisone; HbA1c 5.3 percent; blood pressure 122/78; never smoker. [S]
No statin now; recheck lipids at one year on a low prednisone dose.
Recombinant zoster vaccine dose 2 today.

Glucocorticoids: bone and side effects (Z79.52). Vitamin D 36 on replacement; no hip pain; weight gain and poor sleep expected to ease as the dose falls. [S]
Continue vitamin D3.
Report any hip, groin, or knee pain at once.

Potassium and creatinine after starting losartan

Missed, a deviation from the protocol: the check due two to four weeks after losartan was started was not drawn, because the standing rheumatology orders were for blood counts only. The first potassium, at the sick visit seven and a half weeks after starting, was 4.6 with creatinine unchanged at 0.8, so no harm resulted. Corrective action: a basic metabolic panel was added to the standing orders at that visit, and any dose change will be followed by a check at two weeks
